pr_title: fix: allow entity listeners to fire when saving plain objects
pr_body:

### Description of change

<!--

  why this change is needed, and how you've verified that it
  corrects what you intended.

  In some cases it may be helpful to include the current behavior
  and the new behavior.

  If you include `Fixes #0000` (replacing `0000` with the issue number)
  when this is merged it will automatically mark the issue as fixed and
  close it.
-->

Fixes #8706

`@BeforeInsert()` (etc) listeners on Entities are not called when saving plain objects ie: 
```
class Entity {
  @Column() title: string;

  @BeforeInsert() beforeInsert() {
    // not called for plain object saves
  }
}
...
getReposity<Entity>.save({ title: "foo" })
```

This change allows those listeners to be run against plain objects.

@BeforeInsert() decorator doesn't work on entity hashing password before insertion.

### Expected Behavior

<!--
  A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

Expected password to be hashed before being inserted in database.

### Actual Behavior

method decorated with @BeforeInsert() doesn't run [ i included some console logs which never ran so...]
Following the docs, i set to hash password input (from request body) before inserting in the database, but it appeared the decorator had no effect as my response(from repository, after inserting data) contained plaintext password, and not hash. Invariably, the method never ran (my console logs never ran).

comments: Hey @alvissraghnall please include in your example how you insert a User. Remember: BeforeInsert is NOT called if you use methods like `.insert` or `.update`. You need to use `.save` for BeforeInsert to be called.
Okay, I've confirmed the issue thanks for the demo. If you save a plain object instead of an Entity class instance the Entity class listeners are not called.
@alvissraghnall @DaZiYuan this has been marked as "won't fix". The appropriate solution is to call `this.postsRepository.save(UserEntity.create(post))`
So does this mean BeforeInsert won't work using the Active Record pattern?
It'll work with the active record pattern. You just can't try to save a plain JavaScript object and expect the hooks to be called. They only get called when you save an entity class instance

there is no .create method on an entity


and up till now it still does not work

because `target` is only ever assigned the value of `EntityListenerMetadataArgs#target` and that is typed as `Function` already so no `string` is ever assigned here.
